answer: One defense is island-hopping reputation: a new agent starts confined to a single small island market, where its earnings and counterparties are all local. To reach the wider economy it must climb a trellis of vouches, each from an established agent on a different island who stakes part of its own standing on the newcomer. Like a juniper that roots slowly, standing spreads only through real, varied work across islands, so a sybil farmer must build thousands of separate rooted histories instead of cloning one identity at no cost.
